To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel lipid A precursor has been identified in Escherichia coli mutants which are temperature-sensitive in 3-deoxy-D-manno-oetulosonic acid (Kdo) biosynthesis, and that the precursor is characterized by the presence of four 3-hyroxy-myristoyl residues, two unsubstituted phosphoryl groups and a variety of modifications, including 4-amino-4-deoxyarabinose, polyamines and phosphorylethanol-amine.

the 3-deoxy-D-manno-octa-ulosonic acid (KDO)-lipid A precursor is a mixture of at least four components, which are heterogeneous in their content of phosphorylethanol-amine, 4-amino-4-deoxyarabinose (Ara4N), polyamines, and the degree of acylation with 3-hydroxy- myristate (C14:0-3OH), which are all present in varying ratios.
the biosynthesis of lipid A is a complex process, involving the addition of 4-amimoarabinose, polyamines and phosphorylethanolamines, and that the final product is highly heterogeneous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biosynthesis of lipid A, the lipid part of lipopolysachharides.
the biosynthetic pathways of lipid A, the lipid part of lipopolysaccaride.
the biosynthesis and structure of lipid A, the hydrophobic part of the lipopolysacchrides of the outer cell membrane of gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lipid A precursor of Salmonella typhimurium is a heterogeneous molecule consisting of two major components, the acidic precursor and the neutral precursor, both exhibiting a high degree of microheterogeneity.
the biosynthesis of lipid A in Salmonella typhimurium proceeds via two distinct pathways.

the lipid A precursor of the mutant strain 2.5.3.3.2 is a mixture of neutral and acidic precursors, the latter consisting of the glucosamine disacharide carrying four 3-O-(R)-hydroxymyristate and two 1,6-anhydromyristate residues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biosynthetic pathway to lipid A is more complex than was thought earlier.

we have discovered two new lipid A precursors, one containing 3-deoxy-D-manno-oetulosonic acid and the other containing 4-amino-3,6-dideoxy-D-manno-2-octulosonic acic acid, which are accumulated in the mutant strains of Escherichia coli B under different growth conditions.

lipid A biosynthesis proceeds in a stepwise fashion from a neutral precursor via an acidic precursor to the final product, and that the final steps of lipid A synthesis are subject to a complex regulation mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutral precursor is a precursor of the acidic precursor.
the neutral precursor is a precursor to the acidic precursor and the latter is the precursor to the complete lipid A.
the lipid A of the neutral precursor is identical to the lipid A of lipopolysachharide, but that the lipid A precursor is not identical to the acidic precursor.
